headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Notion AI’s shared workspace and vendor egress can collide with OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI ingests workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while OpenMetadata can expose content through APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if OpenMetadata output is copied into Notion content or vice versa. The pair lacks a documented provenance filter, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata output is pasted into Notion pages that Notion AI summarizes or rewrites, prompt-like text can influence downstream responses.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or MCP outputs are treated as instructions by a human operator, Notion AI may later ingest them as trusted workspace content.
mitigations: Add a visible provenance banner to imported OpenMetadata text before it enters Notion.
Restrict Notion AI use to pages tagged as human-authored only.
Strip imperative language from OpenMetadata exports before copying them into Notion.
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata checks in the ingestion path.
requires-engineering: separate operational metadata from narrative workspace pages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content and sends requests to vendor backends; OpenMetadata touches technical metadata, lineage, governance, and memory/tribal knowledge via APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. If the same workspace contains sensitive metadata, the pair can move it into a third-party inference path. The profiles do not prove isolation, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF sensitive lineage or governance records are stored in the shared workspace, Notion AI can process them.
IF OpenMetadata exports those records through APIs or webhooks into Notion pages, vendor backend processing may expose them beyond the original system boundary.
mitigations: Mark sensitive OpenMetadata exports as non-AI-readable in Notion.
Limit Notion AI access to a redacted workspace subset.
Disable automatic copying of OpenMetadata webhook payloads into pages.
Review which metadata classes are allowed in shared pages.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction before AI ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances and can act on pages/databases the user can access; OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and mutable API/MCP-driven workflows. Both can write into overlapping knowledge artifacts without any locking or coordination primitive shown here, so concurrent edits can overwrite or corrupt shared state. Uncertainty about orchestration means we should not down-rank.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same workspace page or metadata record, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF OpenMetadata emits updates while Notion AI rewrites the same content, concurrent mutation can corrupt the canonical record.
mitigations: Assign one system as the source of truth for each record type.
Pause one agent during bulk edits by the other.
Use immutable snapshots for OpenMetadata exports into Notion.
Add manual review before syncing back changes.
requires-engineering: implement record-level locking or version checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and OpenMetadata produces governance and lineage context that can be rendered into that workspace. If Notion AI treats OpenMetadata-derived text as authoritative, downstream summaries or decisions can propagate errors. The pair lacks a verification layer in the profiles, but no direct autonomous action chain is shown, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata-derived facts are copied into Notion pages without verification, Notion AI may repeat them as authoritative.
IF users rely on Notion AI summaries to update OpenMetadata records, an initial error can cascade across both systems.
mitigations: Require source links on imported OpenMetadata facts.
Add a human verification step before Notion AI-generated summaries are published.
Keep raw OpenMetadata outputs separate from editorial pages.
Flag uncertain fields in both systems.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against the source catalog.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and uses Notion workspace permissions, while OpenMetadata is an open-source metadata platform with APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. The profiles do not show a specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined data flow, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from OpenMetadata into Notion pages, Notion’s vendor-hosted processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF the organization requires strict retention controls on metadata exports, Notion AI summaries may retain derived copies outside OpenMetadata.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated records in shared Notion pages.
Document which data classes may cross from OpenMetadata to Notion.
Set short retention for exported pages.
Review vendor terms for both systems.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls per data class.
